The GTA 6 Ultimate Edition includes the base game and 16 in-game extras , including exclusive vehicles, weapon variants, outfits, shops, and side activities . Some of the bigger additions are the Classic Car Collection, which has you tracking down cars for Wyman to restore, and the ’95 Grotti Cheetah, which you won’t get until Chapter 5.
Rockstar’s edition comparison site also lists the Vintage Vice City Pack and a free month of GTA+ as limited-time bonuses. For a full break down of everything included, check out our GTA 6 Ultimate Edition guide.
Some Ultimate Edition bonuses are available in Chapter 1, with more unlocking in Chapters 2, 4, and 5. Several shops become accessible earlier in the campaign, but it could take around 25 hours or more to reach Chapter 2, depending on how much time you spend exploring.
You could be closer to 60 hours in by the time you reach Chapter 5 and get the ’95 Grotti Cheetah for example. Here’s when each GTA 6 Ultimate Edition bonus becomes available in the story:
Note: Jason’s Dinka Enduro, Crest Kayak, and retro Ganado Build are only usable in Chapter 1. If those were a large part of the why you bought the Ultimate Edition, we recommend using them as much as possible before advancing the story to act 2.
To unlock GTA 6 Ultimate Edition content, you need to progress through the main story. Some bonuses are available automatically in Chapter 1, while others unlock later. For example, the vintage Vice City Style outfits and tattoos for Jason and Lucia become available in Chapter 4.
When certain bonus items unlock, look for a purple icon on your map. These icons often mark where you can find a handful of Ultimate Edition content items.
As someone who reviewed GTA 6 and unlocked all the Ultimate Edition content – in my opinion, yes. I like that the Ultimate Edition rewards you with new stuff as you progress, and gives you actual things to do, especially Wyman’s Classic Car Collection.
If you’re the kind of player who spends hours exploring the map between story missions, those are the extras you would like likely get the most out of. Just know that you won’t be able to access everything from the start. The retro Grotti Cheetah vehicle is a Chapter 5 unlock, and some of Jason’s vehicles are Chapter 1 only.
If you’re buying the edition for one specific bonus, I’d check when you can actually use it before deciding if its worth spending the extra money or not.

Grand Theft Auto 6 arrives on November 19. (Rockstar Games) It's finally here: The long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI drops at midnight local time, so players in New Zealand are already back in Vice City. So far, the reaction is overwhelmingly positive: as of 8:30 a.m. EST, GTA 6 became Metacritic's highest-rated video game in history, based on 167 reviews and counting. Digital marketing firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 pre-orders have already topped $1.65 billion in sales.
If you absolutely can't wait until midnight in your time zone, you can try to set your console's region to New Zealand , but be warned the process is much simpler on an Xbox than it is on a PlayStation5. And some PS5 users have reported their accounts getting banned when they tried this workaround. Since it may cost slightly more to buy the game due to currency conversions, PS5 users around the globe might just want to sit tight until midnight in their home time zone.
PlayStation's network suffered a brief outage Wednesday for some users for about two hours, but by 4 p.m. ET it appeared things were back up and running.

If you don't want to be spoiled, consider getting offline for most of today. Due to the staggered rollout, more regions will get access to GTA 6 throughout the day on Nov. 18. Here's when different areas hit midnight on Nov. 19, 2026:
So far, users who have access to the game are impressed with the high quality of the graphics across the game and how smooth the driving feels, both on the road and on the beach , and how realistic other aspects are like water . So far there haven't been any widespread reports of glitches, but we'll keep an eye out and report back if we see them.

For PS5 users, you'll need to take an extra step before you can play. On Wednesday, Sony issued a system software update for PS5 that it says is required to play GTA 6 . "Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they're ready to play on launch day," the company said in a post on X.

articles.t: PlayStation Network down for thousands as 'GTA 6' launches
articles.chapeau: Downdetector was showing a spike in outages on the PS network
articles.txt:
PlayStation was struggling the day of the GTA 6 launch (REUTERS / Reuters) As users prepared their consoles for the new Grand Theft Auto VI, website outage tracker Downdetector was showing a sharp spike in outages across the PlayStation Network on Wednesday.
Users reported seeing "services are busy" when they tried to sign in to their consoles. Sony needs to verify that a game like GTA 6 was legitimately purchased before one can download it, and verification requires an internet connection. An outage like this could prevent players who pre-ordered the title from downloading and accessing it immediately at launch.
PlayStation didn't immediately reply to a request for comment, but its status page was showing all services up and running in the U.S. Wednesday afternoon by 4 p.m. ET. An earlier message on the page alerted users to a possible issue: "You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience," the notice read.
By 5 p.m. ET, the outage seemed to have come down from its peak although some users were still reporting issues.
GTA6 is set to go live at midnight local time, so users in New Zealand were first to be able to play. The game clocks in at a whopping 212GB, and was already Metacritic's highest-rated video game ever only a few hours into the launch.
Some users in other time zones attempted to set their console's region to New Zealand to get in on the game early, but the process on PS5 is more involved than on Xbox . Plus, PlayStation announced Wednesday that before users could play the game, a software update was necessary. A few users who had tried the time zone workaround reported their accounts had been banned
The outage comes on the heels of several other major internet outages over the past week, that included Apple iCloud , Microsoft , several banks and an FAA full ground stop of all air travel in the U.S. last Friday. There's still no indication that any of the outages are connected, but wary internet denizens wondered if AI could be to blame .

articles.t: GTA 6 cheat codes: There are cheats, but there's a catch
articles.chapeau: They don't work like they used to.
articles.txt:
Throughout their storied history, the Grand Theft Auto games have usually allowed players to skip the stuff they don't like by using cheat codes. There have been codes to inflate in-game wallets, unlock every gun, and even spawn the best vehicles out of thin air. This time, GTA 6 cheat codes take the franchise in a new direction.
Developer Rockstar Games has, by all accounts , created a GTA game that's at least trying to be a little more serious, sincere, and heartfelt than its predecessors. As such, you cannot simply bust out the "all guns" cheat from the start of the game and go on a rampage. According to PC Gamer , the game does have cheats, but they are only accessible after completing all 91 main story missions.
6 Yes, you have to roll credits on the story to use the GTA 6 cheats. Don't get mad at us, get mad at Rockstar.
PC Gamer confirmed that these cheats can't be used in an early-game save, and activating them will prevent the player from saving from that point on.
What's even more interesting: Beating the game doesn't immediately let you use the cheats in question; it merely lets you see a list of them, each with a corresponding in-game challenge that needs to be completed before they can be used. Once a cheat is unlocked, it can then be activated by opening the in-game phone, holding L1 and pressing R1 (or LB and RB on Xbox), and then inputting specific button combos.
For example, the "max ammo" cheat (which presumably just fills up all of your guns) requires the player to win 20 bronze medals or better at shooting ranges. If you want infinite ammo, you'll have to win 25 silver medals or better. To access every explosive weapon, you need to throw 100 grenades.
Each cheat's corresponding in-game challenge is related to what the cheat does, which is a very different approach from how they've worked in the past. You can't say Rockstar isn't trying new things.
So, while you can find lists of cheat codes online, they won't do you any good until you beat the game — at which point you'll get the full list.

Unleashed on Wednesday 13 years after its predecessor, Rockstar Games' wildly anticipated game has landed the highest ever rating on Metacritic . Essentially, it's instantly the best-reviewed game of all time, according to the aggregator site.
GTA 6 has a 99 percent rating on Metacritic, based on 147 critic reviews. This is a weighted average of individual critic scores calculated by Metacritic staff through a complex system involving review detail, publication prestige, and whether the critic has provided a score in their review.
Metacritic predicted GTA 6 would average 96 percent, an already staggering number it's blown out of the water.
In a dramatic twist, GTA 6 also accelerated past the previous #1 ranked game of all time , 1998 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , which has just dominated headlines with Nintendo's new remastered version .
Critics have dubbed GTA 6 everything from "the single most impressive video game I have ever played" to "a masterpiece of open-world design." Meanwhile, players are spending their first few hours with the game and reacting in real-time .

articles.t: Rockstar Leaves Sex Workers Out of Grand Theft Auto for First Time in 25 Years
articles.chapeau: Rockstar Games has explained why GTA 6 is the first Grand Theft Auto title in 25 years without sex workers, citing a focus on Jason and Lucia's relationship.
articles.txt:
For the first time in 25 years, players won’t be able to hire a prostitute in a new Grand Theft Auto game. In a recent interview with Shacknews , Rockstar Games revealed that the feature is missing from GTA 6 because it wanted to focus on Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos’ Bonnie and Clyde story.
“ GTA VI is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run,” explained a Rockstar representative. “While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon — things like [a] wanted system, the radio, robberies, and car theft. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA VI , but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia’s story.”
It’s worth noting that while sex workers are off the table in GTA 6 , strip clubs are alive and well. Tied for the highest-rated game of all time , Rockstar’s latest is currently rolling out globally for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S .

articles.t: PlayStation Network Outage Hits On GTA 6 Release Day Eve
articles.chapeau: PS5 users are reporting widespread technical issues during GTA 6's window as millions try and download Rockstar's open-world shooter.
articles.txt:
What happens when a potential 250 million people try logging into a server at the same time? Problems, that's what. Thursday, Nov. 19 is the official release day for Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, and it appears Sony's platform, commonly known as PlayStation Network, is already buckling the day before under enormous demand for the world's most hyped game.
Many PS5 users tried to plan ahead by preloading the game starting on Nov. 10. Sony surely anticipated potential issues — the company has publicly treated GTA 6 's release as if it were a first-party game — but that did little to prevent outages. Players around the world are facing messages like "Sony services are busy," "Too many failed connection attempts," or a mishmash of different errors. Though Sony's official status tracker currently lists the network as healthy , websites like Down Detector are seeing a sudden jump in reports related to the service. Most PS5 players say they're experiencing login issues with the PlayStation network, but there are also many reports of PSN server connection issues and update and download hiccups.
Whether you've seen codes like WS-116449-5, CE-34861-2, or WS-37505-0, they all point to the same thing: PlayStation's servers are facing serious strain.
Grand Theft Auto 6 Image: Rockstar Games GTA 6 is the follow-up to one of the most successful video games of all time, so the number of people trying to log in at once and download the game is likely massive. In the United States, it's the early afternoon — so many GTA fans probably just got off work and are all trying to do the same thing.
Though GTA 6 is not a multiplayer game that requires an online connection, players must download the title and its mandatory updates before they can enjoy it. This would have been the case even if GTA 6 had been printed on a disc — seemingly all major games require a day-one download for new patches or security reasons, like the recent PS5 jailbreak situation . This means that millions of people are trying to download hundreds of gigabytes of data at the same time, which was never going to end well.
There's no timeline for when PlayStation's servers might stabilize — and by extension, GTA 6 — but given the importance of this release, Sony are undoubtedly working on it.
Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launches on Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

And with Grand Theft Auto VI taking players back to Vice City, the sprawling soundtrack is shaping up to be just as ambitious as the game itself.

Rockstar has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , a 34-track collection of original music arriving Nov. 19, the same day as the game.
The album features an eclectic mix of artists and genres , from hip-hop heavyweights Travis Scott and Cardi B to country star Morgan Wallen and Puerto Rican singer Rauw Alejandro. There's even a collaboration between CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.., and French producer Etienne de Crécy. And somehow, someway, Morgan Wallen's single is the most-streamed track from the soundtrack on Spotify, with more than 25 million streams. Yung Lean, fight back!

The French electronic duo Justice, consisting of Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay, is responsible for the original score of Grand Theft Auto VI .
Rockstar confirmed the news on Oct. 15 alongside the game's launch trailer , which features the debut of Justice's new single, "Flower in a Hurricane," featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and Australian psychedelic rock band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard.
It's a fitting collaboration for a game returning to Vice City, a fictional playground known for its vibrant nightlife and electronic music. Justice's signature blend of distorted synths, disco, and dance music feels particularly suited to Rockstar's radiant criminal underworld.
The duo previously collaborated with Tame Impala on "Neverender" from their 2024 album Hyperdrama . The song won Best Dance/Electronic Recording at the 2025 Grammys.
Rockstar has also confirmed that an official score album is on the way, although additional details, including its release date and tracklist, have yet to be announced.
The fictional radio stations are one of Grand Theft Auto 's most beloved features, and GTA 6 is bringing some major star power to the airwaves.

articles.chapeau: The hacker behind 2022's GTA 6 leaks has pleaded guilty to a series of cyber attacks on Rockstar Games, Uber and more.
articles.txt:
The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.
The GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.
At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.
As the BBC reports , he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.
Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.
"We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar said at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way."
Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up .

articles.txt:
Cybercriminals attempt to cash in on the hype around the game, luring fans with malware-laced downloads and ‘early access’ that doesn’t exist
On November 19 th , 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI will be released for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. But cybercriminals aren’t waiting for launch day. They have long been capitalizing on the hype around what’s arguably the most anticipated game of the decade, using fake leaks, malware-laced downloads, bogus online stores with rock-bottom prices, and fraudulent “early access” schemes to lure eager fans. Security experts at ESET expect such scams to proliferate as the release approaches and the holiday shopping season gets underway.
It’s easy to see why the franchise makes such an attractive lure: Grand Theft Auto is one of the most successful entertainment properties of all time, with more than 470 million units sold worldwide, according to Rockstar Games. Before taking a closer look at the scams tied to GTA VI, let’s establish what Rockstar has actually announced.
Pre-orders opened on June 25 th . According to Rockstar Games’ official pre-order announcement , the Standard Edition is priced at $79.99 in the United States, while the Ultimate Edition costs $99.99. Players who pre-order a digital copy have been able to pre-load the game since November 10 th .
What Rockstar has not announced is just as important, particularly with so many fraudulent offers circulating online: there is currently no official beta, playable demo, or early-access program that would let players start playing GTA VI before release day.
Nor has Rockstar announced a PC version, PC release date, or system requirements. This makes the official information a useful reality check: offers built around a supposed PC version, beta, demo, or early access are promising something Rockstar has never confirmed.
Scam type What to watch out for What attackers are after Credential phishing Fake Rockstar, PlayStation, Xbox, or Steam login pages Gaming-account credentials, passwords, and other personal information Fake beta or early access Invitations to register, log in, pay a fee, or download software to access a nonexistent GTA VI beta, demo, or early-access version Credentials, money, personal data, or malware installation Crypto scams Fake GTA VI giveaways, token airdrops, investment opportunities, or “VIP access” requiring cryptocurrency Cryptocurrency payments or access to victims’ crypto assets Fake stores and pre-orders Cloned or impersonating storefronts offering GTA VI copies, keys, bundles, or versions that have not been officially announced Payment-card details, personal information, or direct payments Malware delivery Fake launchers, leaked builds, beta installers, APKs, cracks, cheats, or preload tools Installation of infostealers, remote-access trojans, or other malware
The enormous anticipation for GTA VI has also made every new leak a magnet for attention. On August 18 th , an entity calling itself CyberLeek began releasing what it claimed was stolen GTA VI material, starting with two gameplay videos and an alleged map of Leonida. By October 12 th , TechWiser had cataloged 19 CyberLeek leaks. The material reportedly included in-game activities, clips featuring cars and aircraft, glimpses of locations and NPC behavior, and eventually story content showing part of Lucia’s prologue. Rockstar has publicly responded to the leaks, describing the release of unfinished material as “heartbreaking” and taking legal action in response.
But CyberLeek wasn't only chasing attention. The campaign also became intertwined with a cryptocurrency called $CYBERLEEK , launched on the Solana blockchain. CyberLeek introduced a token-based voting system in which holders could use $CYBERLEEK to vote on what material would leak next. BitOK , a blockchain analytics company, later investigated the associated on-chain activity and identified several channels through which money flowed into the operation, including token swap fees, voting payments, and direct payments on CyberLeek-linked websites. In one transaction sequence on August 27 th , the wallet that created the token claimed and sold liquidity-pool fees totaling 2,676.67 SOL (approximately $225,000 as of November 11 th , 2026). That said, BitOK cautions against equating individual blockchain flows with net profit or attributing all funds moving through these wallets to a particular person once they have mixed with money from other sources.

Cette affaire est étrange car rappelons que le 14 octobre dernier Cyberleek avait pourtant annoncé abandonner son projet de diffuser une prétendue version complète de GTA 6 . Son objectif financier, fixé à 30 millions de dollars de capitalisation pour sa cryptomonnaie, n’avait pas été atteint.
Dans son message de départ, il affirmait également renoncer à dévoiler la conclusion de l’histoire.
Mais tout vient de changer. Le nouveau communiqué annonce son retour et promet que les prochaines révélations seront détaillées.
Malgré cette déclaration, nous n’avons pas identifié de nouvelle séquence de gameplay pouvant être authentifiée indépendamment. Le site associé à Cyberleek continue de présenter les précédentes publications, notamment celles du 14 octobre.
Il faut également rappeler que plusieurs sites utilisent désormais le nom Cyberleek pour proposer de prétendues versions jouables contre paiement. Dans un tel contexte il est fortement recommandé d’étre très prudent.
Pour revenir à l’affaire de Cyberleek, elle est à surveiller car ce nom est à l’origine de la publication de plusieurs séquences attribuées à des versions de développement de GTA 6. Certaines ont été examinées par des médias spécialisés qui ont jugé que l’authenticité était probable.
Son éventuel retour pourrait donc s’accompagne de nouvelles divulgations serieuses.

articles.chapeau: Leaked nude GTA 6 clips remain unconfirmed and resemble a mod, while the hype fuels scams and a leaker's crypto coin grift.
articles.txt:
The Grand Theft Auto VI nude leaks are back in everyone's feeds and the reaction has gotten out of hand. It certainly doesn't help that Rockstar Games gave us a couple of shower scenes featuring Jason and Lucia in the official launch trailer . However, nothing has changed since we answered the real question . The leaked clips circulating online do not confirm full nudity in the finished game and look like a mod or a dev build.
The reason why we're bringing this up, again, has nothing to do with any of that either: it's that the frenzy is genuinely hurting the people taking part in it.
Think about who benefits every time the nude-leak story spikes. It is not fans. The hunt for a "leaked nude build" is exactly the bait that scammers and malware operators use since the download you are promised is never the game. It is a credential stealer or worse. The grift has gotten specific too. The same leaker is tying nude Lucia clips to a crypto coin , turning the hype into a direct payday. The more the search volume climbs, the more valuable that con becomes.
Who's to say it stops with Cyberleek? Given how much attention Cyberleek has gotten, the scheme could easily inspire countless copycats looking to take advantage of the group of eager fans.
There is a second problem with the pile-on. The thing everyone is reacting to is not confirmed. The several ratings boards across the world flag nudity and strong sexual content , but they do not tell you what any specific scene looks like. People are filling that gap with a leaked clip and calling it proof.
It is also worth a reality check on the shock itself. This is Grand Theft Auto . The series has had strip clubs, sex workers and crude humor for more than two decades. Nudity in a mature, adults-only GTA is not the scandal some reactions treat it as.
But again, none of this is harmless fun with no cost. We have watched the scam warnings spread so far that local news is now telling Miami to be careful . Every surge of nude-leak searching sends more people toward the exact traps those warnings describe. The footage will sort itself out on November 19 when the finished game is out. Unfortunately, the malware, the fake downloads and the crypto grift will not refund anyone in the meantime.
So by all means stay curious about what GTA 6 does with its adults-only rating. Just stop treating a mislabeled clip as the answer. Stop feeding an economy of scammers and grifters who are counting on the obsession.
Veteran · 600 rep Oct 20, 2026 The nude-leak discourse is not about nudity at all but rather for milking hyped-up fans of their money and their passwords.

Grand Theft Auto VI’s most persistent leaker just tried to close the book on a saga that has run for months. Cyberleek framed the release as the final chapter of a leak campaign that had, by its own telling, turned into a cryptocurrency operation. Rockstar Games has not confirmed any of the footage, and the claim that these clips come from the game’s final missions remains unverified.
What makes October 14 different from Cyberleek’s earlier posts is the money trail attached to it. A token called $CYBERLEEK, built on a blockchain and tied directly to the leak campaign, hit a reported peak market capitalization of $7.8 million on October 11, 2026. Within three days, that figure had fallen to roughly $1.2 million, according to IGN, or about $1.7 million per a separate figure reported by Enduins, and later reporting, dated November 13, 2026, still places the coin at approximately $1.2 million in market capitalization. articles.txt:
La communauté du jeu vidéo a récemment été secouée par le retour inattendu de Cyberleek , cette entité anonyme qui avait pris l’habitude de divulguer des informations sensibles concernant les développements internes de Rockstar Games. Après plusieurs jours de silence relatif, ce leaker prolifique a réapparu avec une nouvelle plateforme web et des images inédites tirées de la mission finale de Grand Theft Auto VI .
Cette résurgence soudaine relance le débat éthique autour du piratage numérique et de la préservation de l’expérience joueur, tout en soulevant des questions persistantes quant aux motivations financières derrière ces actions spectaculaires. Les joueurs se demandent désormais si cette promesse de cessation définitive sera tenue ou s’il ne s’agit que d’un artifice marketing supplémentaire destiné à alimenter la spéculation autour des actifs cryptographiques associés.
Contrairement aux précédentes divulgations massives incluant des heures de gameplay brut, Cyberleek a opté pour une approche chirurgicale en publiant exclusivement des séquences de la dernière mission du titre très attendu. L’objectif affiché était de préserver le plaisir de découverte des futurs acheteurs tout en maintenant une pression médiatique maximale sur l’éditeur Take-Two Interactive.
Le leaker a explicitement mentionné détenir les fichiers relatifs à la conclusion narrative globale du jeu mais a choisi de ne pas les diffuser publiquement. Cette décision repose sur un calcul froid : publier la fin aurait causé des dommages irréparables à l’expérience utilisateur, tandis que la retenue actuelle permet de maintenir une forme de levier sans franchir le seuil critique de la ruine totale. La stratégie semble donc évoluer vers une nuisance contrôlée plutôt qu’une destruction ouverte, bien que les intentions profondes restent sujettes à caution.
À LIRE AUSSI : Neuf nouveaux jeux rejoignent le catalogue PlayStation Plus en octobre 2026
Les observateurs avisés ont rapidement noté la coïncidence temporelle entre ces nouvelles fuites et la promotion active d’un jeton numérique non-fongible baptisé « CL ». Cyberleek rejette catégoriquement toute accusation de spéculation financière pure, qualifiant le token de simple outil de collecte de dons destinés à financer ses activités futures.
Néanmoins, la corrélation directe entre la visibilité accrue apportée par les leaks et la capitalisation boursière volatile de ce meme-coin suggère une dynamique économique sous-jacente indéniable. Le leaker accuse les sceptiques, notamment certains créateurs de contenu YouTube, de cynisme aveugle face à sa prétendue démarche philanthropique envers la communauté des joueurs.
Il affirme agir pour protéger l’intégrité du divertissement contre les abus corporatifs, tout en exploitant paradoxalement l’écosystème spéculatif des cryptomonnaies pour soutenir son infrastructure technique coûteuse et complexe.
Au cœur de cette saga digitale se trouve un mystérieux projet parallèle, distinct de Rockstar, nécessitant des ressources matérielles considérables et une durée de développement estimée à plusieurs années. Pour concrétiser cette ambition, Cyberleek avait conditionné la publication d’une build complète du jeu au franchissement d’un palier symbolique de trente millions de dollars en capitalisation boursière du memecoin associé.
Cet objectif ambitieux n’a jamais été atteint, la valeur du jeton stagnants autour d’un million de dollars seulement. Face à cet échec financier cuisant, le leaker a annoncé honorer ses engagements contractuels implicites en refusant de télécharger anonymement plus de deux cents gigaoctets de données risquées.
Cette posture rigide masque mal une déception profonde vis-à-vis d’une audience jugée trop frileuse pour soutenir pleinement ses initiatives audacieuses et potentiellement lucratives.
À LIRE AUSSI : Rockstar garantit un développement plus rapide pour son prochain titre
Malgré les promesses solennelles de retrait définitif formulées dans le communiqué officiel, la prudence demeure de mise parmi les analystes du secteur vidéoludique. Avec encore plus d’un mois avant la sortie officielle de Grand Theft Auto VI , il paraît improbable que cette source d’information cesse totalement ses activités perturbatrices.
Le style rédactionnel particulier, marqué par une utilisation excessive de la voix passive et une structure syntaxique hachée, confirme la continuité de l’auteur principal derrière ces publications successives.

articles.txt:
Cyberleek, the anonymous account behind months of Grand Theft Auto VI leaks, says it is done. On October 14, 2026, the leaker posted a three-part message titled “End of the road,” announcing it will not release a full game build, will not post the game’s ending, and does not plan further early gameplay leaks. The post marks the clearest signal yet that the long-running GTA 6 leak saga, which has rattled Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive for the better part of a year, may finally be winding down.
Whether that holds is a separate question. Cyberleek has reversed course before, and its claimed access to a development build and to the game’s ending, made on October 13 and 14, 2026, has not been independently confirmed. The message itself said only that the leaks had stopped “for now.” Still, the announcement reframes a leak campaign that previously threatened to dump an entire playable build onto torrent sites. Instead, the leaker is walking away, at least for now, while keeping a handful of final-mission clips online as what it calls proof of access.

According to the October 14 post, Cyberleek broke its farewell statement into three distinct parts. The first addressed the fate of the alleged full game build, the second covered the ending and story content, and the third offered a handful of final clips described as proof rather than spoilers. Kotaku reported on the message under the headline “GTA 6 Leaker Announces They Won’t Release The Full Game” , framing it as the leaker calling a stop to the campaign, at least for the time being.
Cyberleek had previously floated a conditional threat: if a crypto token tied to the account hit a $30 million market cap, the full build would go out, story mode included, all the way to the credits. In its own words from that earlier post, “Here’s the deal, nice and clean. CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out, full story mode, played to the end, credits and all,” as Gadgets360 reported at the time. That target was never reached, and the October 14 message closes the loop on it.
Cyberleek’s stated reasoning centers on risk versus reward. Uploading a claimed 200+ GB playable build anonymously, a release Mashable reported Cyberleek threatened on October 12, 2026, carries real exposure. PCMag reported the playable build was advertised as over 200GB in October 2026, and Mashable reported that an alleged development build was offered behind a $40 paywall that same month. The leaker framed the payoff as only worth it if the associated cryptocurrency reached its $30 million market-cap target and funded whatever project sat behind the threat. With the target missed, the math apparently stopped working. The account has made no claim about a PC build timeline, pricing, or file size beyond what it has already posted, and none of those specifics are confirmed by any outlet covering the story.
This is a notable shift from the tone Cyberleek struck in earlier posts, which read more like negotiation tactics aimed at Take-Two than a farewell. articles.txt:
L’affaire Cyberleek connaît un nouveau rebondissement. Alors que le responsable présumé des nombreuses fuites de GTA 6 annonçait mettre fin à ses publications, un nouveau message vient contredire cette décision.
Sur son site, Cyberleek affiche désormais une annonce intitulée “DEVELOPMENT BUILD IS OUT”. Il affirme proposer une version de développement du prochain jeu de Rockstar Games pour 40 dollars. Cette nouvelle déclaration intervient quelques heures seulement après son message The End of t he Road , dans lequel il expliquait renoncer à diffuser sa prétendue build complète.

Dans son message du 14 octobre, l’entité expliquait donc qu’elle ne publierait pas la build, évoquant notamment les risques associés à la distribution anonyme de plus de 200 Go de données. Mais quelques heures plus tard, changement de discours.

Cyberleek annonce l’arrêt de sa campagne contre Rockstar Games et Take-Two Interactive. Dans un communiqué en trois parties publié le 14 octobre, intitulé “ La fin de la route “, le groupe anonyme affirme abandonner la publication d’une soit disant version complète et jouable de GTA 6.
Cette décision n’est pas une surprise puisqu’elle a été conditionnée à l’échec d’une opération liée à une cryptomonnaie. Le groupe voulait porter sa capitalisation à 30 millions de dollars , un seuil qui n’a pas été atteint.
Cyberleek avait conditionné la publication de l’intégralité de la campagne solo à cette valorisation. Il avait également proposé de renoncer à la diffusion si Take-Two acceptait de commercialiser le jeu sur disques physiques et présentait des excuses publiques.
Pour expliquer cette marche arrière, le groupe met en avant les difficultés d’une mise en ligne anonyme de plus de 200 Go de données. Il estime que les risques associés ne se justifient pas sans avoir atteint son objectif financier.
Enfin le groupe assure aussi détenir la fin de GTA 6, tout en affirmant avoir choisi de ne pas la dévoiler. Selon son communiqué, certains extraits récemment diffusés proviendraient des missions finales, mais auraient été sélectionnés pour éviter les révélations importantes sur l’intrigue.
Malgré l’annonce de son retrait, Cyberleek conserve un moyen de pression. Il prend la forme d’un prétendu “ interrupteur de l’homme mort “, censé déclencher la publication de spoilers si le groupe était ciblé.

On August 18, an unidentified person or group going by the name "Cyberleek" began sharing what appeared to be Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay clips on the internet.
The internet was naturally skeptical, but the footage was hard to fault: It looked authentic, showing mundane GTA 6 gameplay featuring its male protagonist, Jason. In one clip the player shot a basketball outside of the same house we've seen in the trailers, and in another he did some typical GTA random-civilian-murdering.
A day later, Cyberleek dropped two more videos , both of which also looked legit. At the same time, the clips were being stricken from social media on copyright grounds—the only public response from Take-Two and Rockstar so far.
The fifth video Cyberleek released ended with a twist: the player writing the word "LEEK" into the side of a building with bullet holes. These are not, it turns out, clips taken by GTA 6 testers and found on an unsecured server, as many assumed. Cyberleek has (or had) access to a build of GTA 6 , or a portion of it.
We don't know exactly how Cyberleek is getting their clips. The footage of them shooting "LEEK" into a wall indicates they have or had access to a playable build, but it is not necessarily the full game. It's notable that GTA 6's other protagonist, Lucia, has not shown up in the clips.
It does seem that these clips are from a relatively recent build, however. In one of the clips, the in-game radio is playing "Sports Car" by Tate McRae, which released in January 2025.

Cyberleek has made common consumer rights complaints their justification for the leaks: "Publishers sell licenses and call them purchases. They ship unfinished games and call them living services. They lock content on discs and call it DLC. They kill games and keep the money. Every year anti-consumerism tightens its grip, and every year gamers get less for what they pay."
At a glance, Cyberleek's complaints seem typical, but two of the three demands they've put forward strike me as slightly strange choices.
The demands are: no more digital preorders, no more selling DLC already contained in the base game files, and mandatory "offline fallback states" for the singleplayer components of games.
The third demand is the most expected, and is similar though not identical to the demand of the Stop Killing Games movement (which has disavowed the leaker ).
The other two, however, don't seem like the kind of core issues most people would choose if they were putting forward their three biggest gripes about the games industry in 2026.
On-disc DLC—where add-on content is included in the base game's files, but inaccessible without paying extra—was a big controversy around 10-15 years ago, but is much less relevant in today's mostly discless world.
The complaint that preorders don't really mean anything when you're not preordering an actual physical disc is also valid, but seems like a roundabout way to complain about the heart of the issue: The end of physical media, which has been a hot button topic following Sony's announcement that it will cease disc production .
I'm not sure you can rally a movement behind ending digital preorder bonuses and preloading: GTA 6 itself has already enjoyed an "unprecedented" number of preorders . You can definitely rally a movement behind seeing more GTA 6 leaks, though

articles.t: Cyberleek says 'GTA 6' leaks are over, warns of dead man's switch
articles.chapeau: Sounds like we're done with all of this.
articles.txt:
Cyberleek might finally, mercifully, be done sharing Grand Theft Auto VI clips.
On the Cyberleek website, as spotted by Reddit and cited by Kotaku , the person or group of people behind all the recent GTA 6 leaks you may have seen on your social feeds appeared to call it quits. According to the post, the leaker's threat to release a full build of the game will seemingly go unfulfilled, as they did not meet the $30 million market value goal for their memecoin. However, the post did imply that there is a "dead man's switch" in place that will release the build, or some other kind of spoiler content, if anyone tries to "remove" Cyberleek.
"CL has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly - but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong," the post said. "Take-Two would show CL no mercy - why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished. Proof: the latest leek - clips from the final missions, out of context, revealing nothing. The dead man's switch is active - story spoilers only. Left alone, it never fires. Whoever removes CL chooses it."
Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive, the makers of GTA 6, have already subpoenaed Google, Microsoft, X, and Discord in their efforts to unmask and stop Cyberleek.
The leaker's post went on to defend the meme-coin at the center of the leaks, claiming it was not a "rugpull."
“CL was transparent about the token from day one: a donation, never an investment," Cyberleek said. "It changed nothing – influencers decided the story before the facts arrived. The Edict stands. The leeks stop here. For now.”
Over the past few months, the anonymous leaker has posted roughly 20 or so out-of-context clips that mostly showed the game's protagonists driving around and/or beating up NPCs, although the leaker did start sharing some story spoilers . By the end, they were showing both protagonists rendered completely nude, but it's arguable that none of the leaks told us as much about the game as Rockstar's own Netflix trailer did in August.
Regardless, it seems like this Cyberleek saga is over for the time being. It's only about a month until the game launches on Nov. 19, and gamers can preorder the game ahead of its release.

articles.t: GTA 6 : le hacker Cyberleek met fin aux fuites et renonce à publier le jeu complet
articles.chapeau: Le leaker Cyberleek annonce l'arrêt de ses fuites de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) et renonce à publier la version complète du jeu qu'il affirme détenir.
articles.txt:
Sony détaille un peu plus la rétrocompatibilité sur sa PlayStation 5. Il sera possible de jouer à la grande majorité des jeux PlayStation 4 sur la PS5, mais tous ne seront pas compatibles.
Le leaker Cyberleek annonce l’arrêt de ses fuites de Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA 6 ) et renonce à publier la version complète du jeu qu’il affirme détenir . Dans un message publié aujourd’hui sur son site, le hacker explique que son objectif financier n’a pas été atteint, tout en laissant planer la possibilité de nouvelles révélations.
Dans un message en trois parties intitulé The End of the Road , Cyberleek confirme qu’il ne publiera pas la version jouable complète de GTA 6 qu’il prétend avoir en sa possession. Le hacker affirmait auparavant pouvoir diffuser l’intégralité du mode histoire, jusqu’au générique de fin, si sa cryptomonnaie atteignait 30 millions de dollars. Cet objectif n’ayant pas été atteint, la publication est annulée.
Cyberleek avance également un argument pratique : mettre en ligne anonymement un fichier de plus de 200 Go présenterait des risques importants, sans contrepartie financière suffisante. L’existence de cette version complète et sa taille restent toutefois non vérifiées. Aucun élément indépendant ne permet de confirmer que le pirate possède réellement une copie jouable intégrale du prochain jeu de Rockstar Games.
L’annonce intervient après plusieurs semaines de leaks d’extraits de gameplay issus d’une version de développement . Le leaker avait notamment publié une longue séquence montrant Jason et Lucia, les deux protagonistes, ainsi que différentes situations de jeu. Certaines images semblaient provenir de missions avancées de l’histoire.
Cyberleek affirme également connaître le dénouement du jeu, mais assure avoir choisi de ne pas le révéler afin de préserver l’expérience des joueurs. Il soutient que les dernières séquences publiées proviennent de missions finales, présentées sans leur contexte narratif pour éviter de dévoiler les principaux rebondissements.
Le message contient toutefois une réserve importante : « Les fuites s’arrêtent ici. Pour l’instant »/ Cyberleek affirme aussi avoir activé un mécanisme de publication différée qui déclencherait la diffusion de spoilers s’il était pris pour cible par les autorités. Cette menace entretient donc l’incertitude sur la suite de l’affaire, malgré l’annonce d’un arrêt des publications de leaks.
La campagne de Cyberleek associait les révélations sur GTA 6 à une cryptomonnaie portant son nom. En échange d’une capitalisation de 30 millions de dollars, le leaker promettait de publier le jeu complet. Il avait également posé une autre condition à Take-Two, maison mère de Rockstar Games : sortir le jeu sur disque physique et présenter des excuses publiques. Pour rappel, Grand Theft Auto VI sera uniquement disponible en version numérique . Cyberleek rejette les accusations selon lesquelles cette opération aurait constitué une escroquerie destinée à faire monter artificiellement la valeur du token avant sa revente.
Rockstar Games n’a pas publiquement commenté cette dernière annonce. Sa maison mère, Take-Two, cherche néanmoins à identifier le ou les responsables des fuites, notamment au moyen de procédures judiciaires visant à obtenir des informations auprès de plateformes en ligne. Discord et Microsoft font partie des plateformes visées . La publication du jeu complet n’est donc plus à l’ordre du jour selon Cyberleek, mais rien ne garantit que les fuites cesseront définitivement avant la sortie officielle de GTA 6 , prévue le 19 novembre sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X/S.
Merci de nous avoir signalé l'erreur, nous allons corriger cela rapidement.

articles.t: Le token CYBERLEEK chute de 40 % alors que le leaker de GTA 6 lance de nouvelles menaces
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek menace de révéler la fin de GTA 6 s
articles.txt:
Le token CYBERLEEK chute de 40 % alors que le leaker de GTA 6 lance de nouvelles menaces Luis Blanco 15 octobre 2026 3 min de lecture TTWO Le token CYBERLEEK chute de 41 % alors que le leaker de GTA 6 menace de révéler la fin. Photo by BeInCrypto Cyberleek, le leaker pseudonyme de GTA 6, affirme que la fin du jeu sera révélée s'il se fait attraper, une menace qui survient alors que le token lié à ses fuites dégringole.
Le token a chuté de 41 % mercredi, et la sortie de GTA 6 est désormais prévue dans environ cinq semaines.
Cyberleek a publié un dernier message ce matin, déclarant que la version complète restera privée. Le compte affirme posséder déjà la fin du jeu.
À titre de preuve, le compte a montré des extraits hors contexte des missions finales de l'histoire. Plutôt que de tout rendre public, le leaker propose un « dead man's switch » qui dévoilerait la fin s'il venait à être arrêté.
Le leaker estime que Take-Two, la maison-mère de Rockstar Games, a déjà assez souffert, et que la publication de spoilers nuirait à l'expérience des joueurs.
Le jeu est toujours prévu pour le 19 novembre. Chris Bratt, du média People Make Games, indique qu'un tribunal réunissant Rockstar et 34 employés licenciés se tiendra les 17 et 18 novembre.
Certains utilisateurs sur X spéculent que Cyberleek pourrait faire partie des employés licenciés, même si rien ne vient le confirmer. Cela dit, les extraits sont diffusés hors contexte, ce qui rend leur authenticité difficile à vérifier.
Le leaker publie du contenu inédit de GTA 6 et associe chaque nouvelle fuite à la valorisation du token CYBERLEEK. En effet, son prix détermine combien du jeu parvient jusqu'aux fans.
CYBERLEEK a chuté de 41 % en 24 heures et s'échange autour de 0,00155 $, selon les données de CoinGecko. Ce prix se situe environ 96 % en dessous de son record historique.
Des paliers de valorisation ont rythmé chaque publication depuis le début. Les premières fuites avaient propulsé le token jusqu'à 40 millions de dollars de capitalisation.
Le token a ensuite grimpé de 200 % en deux jours, sans toutefois retrouver ce pic initial. Cyberleek a alors décidé de ne plus publier l'intégralité du contenu. Sa capitalisation boursière dépasse à peine le million de dollars, très loin de l'objectif des 30 millions.
La feuille de route relie les prochaines fuites à l'atteinte de nouveaux paliers de plusieurs millions de dollars de capitalisation. Le leaker précise que les révélations régulières vont cesser, car le token performe mal.

articles.t: Cyberleek publie sa dernière fuite sur GTA 6, renonçant à mettre en ligne une version PC ou des spoilers sur l’histoire
articles.chapeau: Après avoir publié une série de fuites sur GTA 6, Cyberleek affirme avoir mis en ligne ses dernières images. Comme l’objectif en cryptomonnaie n’a pas été atteint, les soutiens ne verront ni révélations sur l’histoire ni version PC jouable. Un extrait de gameplay, censé provenir des dernières missions, commence avec Lucia dans un salon de coiffure.
articles.txt:
Les joueurs inquiets des spoilers sur l’histoire avant la date de sortie de GTA 6 peuvent pousser un soupir de soulagement. Après avoir échoué à atteindre une capitalisation boursière de 30 millions de dollars pour un meme coin, Cyberleek affirme avoir publié sa dernière fuite. Les sites de piratage ne verront pas non plus la version PC jouable que Cyberleek menaçait de mettre en ligne. Des séquences centrées sur Lucia , provenant prétendument des dernières missions, accompagnaient le message.
Cyberleek a commencé sa dernière mise à jour en défendant les précédentes ventes massives de cryptomonnaies . Le bourreau de Rockstar soutient que tous les objectifs précédemment atteints ont donné lieu aux fuites de GTA 6 promises. La personne à l’origine des fuites estime avoir été injustement tenue responsable d’une « cascade » de ventes effectuées par d’autres détenteurs.
Les spoilers sur l’histoire sont également exclus, car ils « gâcheraient l’expérience des joueurs, qui n’ont rien fait de mal ». Même si cela porterait gravement préjudice à l’éditeur, Cyberleek déclare : « Take-Two a été suffisamment puni. »
Partager la version PC de plus de 200 Go aurait été encore plus désastreux pour Take-Two et Rockstar Games. Toutefois, sans atteindre l’objectif de 30 millions de dollars en cryptomonnaies, l’individu a estimé que le risque n’en valait pas la peine.
Réaffirmant que les dons étaient une marque de soutien plutôt qu’un investissement, Cyberleek promet que les « fuites s’arrêtent ici. Pour l’instant. » On ignore si Cyberleek refera surface avant la date de sortie de GTA 6 . Quoi qu’il en soit, les fans disposent d’un dernier extrait de gameplay d’environ 4 minutes intitulé « The End of the Road ». "Don't Stop Believin’" de Journey accompagne l’ensemble des images.
Lucia entre d’abord dans un salon de coiffure où des PNJ discutent en arrière-plan. Alors que la partenaire de Jason quitte le commerce, elle frappe le caissier et le dévalise. Une grande partie de la fuite de GTA 6 porte sur des changements de coiffure, puis sur l’achat d’ articles dans une boutique de vêtements.
Les spectateurs ont tout de même un aperçu d’un mini-jeu qui sera disponible. Au cours de ce qui semble être une mission, Lucia joue au billard dans un bar et gagne une petite somme d’argent. Avant la fin de l’extrait, les joueurs découvrent un plan cinématique d’un pont. La vidéo montre différents endroits de Leonida , puis passe à un quartier résidentiel qui semble se trouver dans un autre État que la Floride.

articles.txt: Le leaker de GTA 6 à la tête de poireau aurait publié une nouvelle vidéo de gameplay du jeu ; cette fois-ci, elle montrerait Lucia entièrement nue , une manœuvre visant à promouvoir une fois de plus sa propre cryptomonnaie. Pour autant, certains soupçonnent désormais le dénommé Cyberleek d'utiliser un debug mode ou des codes de triche pour déshabiller Jason et Lucia, et estiment ainsi que ces images ne reflètent pas fidèlement l'expérience du jeu final. articles.t: Cyberleek Returns, Posts More 'GTA VI' Footage, Promises Not to Return Again
articles.chapeau: We can but hope.
articles.txt:
For anyone worried that it’s been several hours since we last heard from valiant pro-physical media warrior and budding crypto entrepreneur Cyberleek , fear not: they’re back. And if you’re wondering whether all the attention of the past few weeks has gone to their alliumal head, consider this: Cyberleek is still referring to themselves in the third person. Readers can draw their own conclusions.
The prolific leaker returned overnight with a new website, a new Grand Theft Auto VI leak, and an update. This, quoth Cyberleek, is the end. If so, they’re going out with a bang: the leak featured footage of the game’s final mission, shorn of context so they wouldn’t risk ruining gamers’ funsies. Cyberleek is also saying that they have footage of the game’s ending, but they’re not going to post it: “[Cyberleek] has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly – but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy – why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished.”
Cyberleek: doin’ it for the gamers. Some, however, might suggest that Cyberleek is in fact doing it for the cash. After all, the leaks have coincided with the launch of a memecoin, and all the publicity has driven a whole heap of people toward what would otherwise be just another forgotten slice of the blockchain.
Cyberleek, of course, has no time for such quibblers, calling them godless cynics—or, worse, YouTubers —who don’t understand what Cyberleek is doing for the kids. “The token was only a donation. Never an investment.” Which, I mean, fair: anyone who considers a memecoin linked to an anonymous hacker whose entire public presence involves leaks from a game whose release is a month away an “investment” needs their head examined.
Anyway, it turns out that Cyberleek is disappointed with their flock. The last leak made reference to a secret project for which they were seeking funding: “Cyberleek has a project. Not Rockstar related. Gaming related. It needs expensive hardware. Months to set up. Years to run. Full time.” Well, despite estimates that the coin has allowed Cyberleek to cash out somewhere in the order of $250,000, it seems that this wasn’t enough.
In a sort of pseudo-Kickstarter structure, Cyberleek tied various milestones to the memecoin’s market capitalization, including a release of the entire game if the market cap hit $30m. It… did not. At all. The coin’s market cap is currently sitting at around $1m, which just goes to show that there are only so many people with Pepe avatars you can fleece at any given moment.
But Cyberleek isn’t mad; they’re just disappointed: “The [milestone] was not reached, so no build. Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk – worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project. Terms honored as written. Sad.” That’s right: no game for you, and it’s your own fault. I hope you’re happy.
As ever, it’s not clear whether Cyberleek is one person, multiple people, or a state of mind, but the prose in last night’s announcement certainly matched the sort of sub-LinkedIn style of previous posts, with its heavy use of the passive voice and strange, stop-start sentence structure, so it seems reasonable to assume that whoever was behind the previous leaks was also behind this one. Is this the last we’ll hear from them? With over a month until GTA VI launches, that feels unlikely, but we’ll see.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' file size: Cyberleek reveals eye-watering storage requirements
articles.chapeau: Take it with a grain of salt, of course.
articles.txt:
The person leaking a bunch of gameplay videos of Grand Theft Auto VI may have just revealed the most useful information in all of their leaks.
On the Cyberleek website (per our colleagues at PCMag ), one of the latest updates included a threat to release a full build of the game in some form if people on the internet raised the leaker's crypto memecoin to a $30 million market cap. The coin has since crashed and looks like it's not going to get anywhere close to that level, but more importantly, the update included a file size for the playable build they have evidently been taking clips from: 200GB.
That's obviously a huge number, and makes up more than 20 percent of the usable storage space on a base PS5 or Xbox Series X console. Perhaps surprisingly, it's not as big as some other games, as recent Call of Duty titles clear 200GB by a good margin. But it would still be one of the biggest single-player file sizes we've seen yet, and speaks to the scale and scope of GTA 6 .
Of course, this should be taken with at least a tiny bit of skepticism. We don't know much about the build Cyberleek has been leaking footage from. If they do indeed have the full game on hand, it could be an older build that hasn't been fully optimized yet, so the true GTA 6 file size could theoretically be smaller once the actual game comes out on Nov. 19.

CYBERLEEK Token Crashes 40% as GTA 6 Leaker Makes New Threats Luis Blanco October 15, 2026 2 min read TTWO +8.10% CYBERLEEK Token Tumbles 41% as GTA 6 Leaker Threatens Ending. Photo by BeInCrypto Cyberleek, the pseudonymous GTA 6 leaker, says the game's ending will surface if they are caught, a threat that arrives as the token behind their leaks tumbles.
The token fell 41% on Wednesday, and the GTA 6 release is now about five weeks away.
Cyberleek posted the latest message this morning, saying the full build will stay private. The account says it already has the ending.
As evidence, the account showed out-of-context clips from the final story missions. Rather than release it, the leaker proposes a dead man's switch that would spoil the ending if they are caught.
The leaker argues that Take-Two, parent company of Rockstar Games, has suffered enough, and that spoilers would damage the experience.
The game is still scheduled for November 19. Chris Bratt of People Make Games says a tribunal between Rockstar and 34 fired workers will meet on November 17 and 18.
Some X users speculate that the fired employees may include Cyberleek, though nothing confirms the idea. The clips, however, are shown without context, which makes their authenticity hard to verify.
The leaker releases unreleased GTA 6 material and ties each new drop to the market value of the CYBERLEEK token. In effect, its price decides how much of the game reaches fans.
CYBERLEEK fell 41% in 24 hours and trades near $0.00155, according to CoinGecko data. That price sits roughly 96% below its all-time high.
Valuation milestones have shaped every release since the start. The first leaks pushed the token to a $40 million market cap.
The token then climbed 200% in two days, yet it still fell short of that earlier peak. Cyberleek responded by withholding the full build. Its market cap sits a little above $1 million, far below the $30 million target.
The roadmap ties future drops to milestones of several million dollars in market cap. Regular releases will stop, the leaker says, because the token is performing poorly.

articles.t: GTA 6 Cyberleek update: Leaker linked GTA 6 reveals to crypto play. It’s crashing spectacularly.
articles.chapeau: The Cyberleek memecoin is now plunging further and further.
articles.txt:
As Mashable and our colleagues at PCMag just reported, Grand Theft Auto VI leakers Cyberleek have seemingly abandoned their threats to leak a full build of the game – at least for now.
Why? Because the leakers had claimed that the release of the leaked build was tied to their memecoin. If GTA 6 fans pumped Cyberleek's cryptocurrency, they would receive the leaked game build as a reward.
That play failed spectacularly for Cyberleek. In fact, it seems to have fully backfired.
The Cyberleek memecoin's market cap hit a high of $7.8 million on October 11, shortly after the leakers claimed they would release the full build of GTA 6 supposedly in their possession. The catch? The Cyberleek memecoin had to hit a market cap of $30 million first. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile
While some GTA 6 fans appeared to have bought into the memecoin in an attempt to hit Cyberleek's goal, $7.8 million is still far short of the $30 million the leakers wanted. And since then, as it became obvious that most GTA 6 fans weren't going to give in to Cyberleek's demands, the memecoin has plunged even further, with a current market cap of $1.17 million.
Critics of Cyberleek celebrated the memecoin's failure, calling it a scam.
Cyberleek had been successful with their memecoin play before, giving those who bought their memecoin exclusive access to polls that determined what GTA 6 footage the leakers would release next.
However, it seems Cyberleek overplayed their hand this time around, and the full build, which they claim is 200GB, appears to be staying under wraps for now.
With that said, Cyberleek is still using their supposed access to a full build of GTA 6 to try to escape legal action from Take-Two, the parent company of GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games. The leakers claim that there is a "dead-man's switch" that will automatically release the ending of the game if there is an attempt to take down Cyberleek.
